versions.title_at_revision: Verify that the propeller can tolerate bird strikes.
versions.text: Verify that the propeller can tolerate bird strikes. FAA Doc: 14CFR references: 35.36

Criterion: Verify that the propeller can tolerate bird strikes. Standard: The propeller blades and spinner are capable of withstanding the impact of a four-pound bird at the critical location(s) and critical flight condition(s) of the air vehicle without causing a structural failure or inability to control the propeller. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, and review of documentation. Component/rig tests or analysis based on relevant acceptable birdstrike tests verify the structural integrity and controllability of the propeller and spinner under bird ingestion conditions. Reference: 14 CFR 35.36

Standard: The propeller blades and spinner can withstand the impact of a four-lb bird at the propeller and spinner critical location(s) (e.g., highest stress, most damaging vibratory locations) over the range of flight conditions expected of the air vehicle without causing a structural failure or inability to control the propeller throughout the flight and ground envelope per the 7.5.2 for the stated life documented in technical data. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., propeller control system design documentation, hardware drawings, system configuration descriptions, design data records, test reports, or other substantiating records and reports) to verify the design. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is conducted to determine the critical impact conditions affecting propeller structural integrity and control, including both impact location and operating conditions. Structural analysis verifies the structural integrity and controllability. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Component and rig tests, including test at the determined critical impact conditions, verify the structural integrity and controllability.
